title: Fixed 4.03-day fits do not confirm an extra Ross 128 signal in 305 HARPS exposures
abstract: We test the reported 4.03-day residual signal of Ross 128 in HARPS-RVBank version 02. After calendar-year offsets and two waves for the known planet, the corrected SERVAL amplitude is 0.354 m/s. Conditional residual sign tests give tail fractions of 0.206 to 0.328 for three time-bin lengths. An archival fit reduces later error by 0.49 percent in SERVAL but raises it by 2.96 percent in DRS. A restricted 3.8-to-4.25-day search gives different peaks in the two reductions and no stable evidence across noise rules. Recovery of added 0.5 m/s waves is limited. These tests do not confirm an extra signal, exclude a weak planet, or identify a physical cause. The reductions share spectra. There is no independent instrument confirmation. Code, aggregate evidence, input hashes, a figure and retrieval steps are included. External source records remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Restricted period scans and transfer of a fixed 4.03-day wave between archival and post-warmup observations. The ranges hold the training wave fixed and omit its estimation error.

citations.reason: Reports the unresolved 4.03-day signal and possible activity link. We test a fixed wave in a different public reduction.
Exact external input; SHA-256 and retrieval recipe are in provenance.json.
Prior campaign time-transfer test for another HARPS star. No code or data are reused.
